decision.observation: 7 mph, gear R, timer 14:19.440, all dots pale. The car has backed off the sapling a metre or so and sits at the right edge of the gravel, nose still up-frame toward that trunk; the road curves left ahead, so backing further would put the car further down the straight (behind) rather than helping.
decision.hypothesis: The nose only just cleared the trunk. A short extra reverse should give enough clearance to then aim forward with a left steer; alternatively, staying put risks re-pinning on the same trunk when W is pressed.
decision.memory: This right-edge sapling re-pins on repeated forward attempts; after reversing, the very next forward input must angle away from it.
